preamble: The shift from the open central vowel [a] to the open-mid back unrounded vowel [ʌ] (the caret) is a backing and raising of the low vowel. In the Godié branch of Eastern Kru, Proto-Eastern Kru *a gave a new central-back vowel ʌ in many words (*ka³ 'have' > kʌ³), while peripheral /a/ was also kept.

examples.note: Superscript digits are Marchese Zogbo's tone levels; the reconstruction rests on Dida, Neyo, Guibéroua and Daloa Bété forms.
Marchese Zogbo finds few conditioning factors; Godié keeps peripheral /a/ alongside the new central vowel /ʌ/.

sources: Marchese Zogbo, L. (2019). Central vowels in the Kru language family: Innovation and areal spreading. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.3367199
